facts.raw_span: a 1-year history of pain and swelling around his right ankle
bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
the ankle and subtalar joints had a full range of motion
Complete blood count was within normal limits
erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 68 mm at the first hour
a submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin
a diagnosis of Brodie’s abscess was made
curettage was performed under spinal anesthesia via an anterior approach
curetted material was sent for histopathological and microbiological assessment

concepts.why: The patient's 1-year history of pain and swelling around the ankle, bony thickening, and lytic lesion with a sclerotic margin are consistent with Brodie's abscess, a type of subacute osteomyelitis.
The patient's long-standing symptoms and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate suggest a chronic infection, which is consistent with chronic osteomyelitis.
The lytic lesion with a sclerotic margin could be suggestive of a bone tumor, such as Ewing's sarcoma, although the diagnosis of Brodie's abscess was made.
The patient's pain and bony thickening could be consistent with an osteoid osteoma, a type of benign bone tumor.
The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with subacute osteomyelitis, which is a type of bone infection.
The patient's long-standing symptoms and laboratory results suggest a chronic inflammatory process, which could be consistent with a chronic inflammatory bone disease.
The lytic lesion with a sclerotic margin could be suggestive of a bone cyst, although the diagnosis of Brodie's abscess was made.
The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with osteomyelitis, which is a type of bone infection.
